clue.text: Mostly an obvious sort of plate.

indicators.note: mostly means nearly all of the word, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: patent means plainly evident or obvious

explanation.surface: Someone remarks that a dish is mostly of a very ordinary, obvious kind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mostly' trims the last letter from PATENT, leaving the name of the small dish used at the Eucharist.
explanation.definitionFit: A paten is the shallow dish, usually gold or silver, that holds the bread during Communion.

clue.text: Stamps stamps

explanation.surface: A bare repetition, as if someone were stamping twice.
explanation.walkthrough: The same word is used in two senses: as a verb (marks a letter with the post office's date and place) and as a noun (those official franking marks themselves).
explanation.definitionFit: The post office franks letters with cancellation marks; doing so, and the marks it leaves, are both called by this word.

clue.text: Flap or drum

parts.note: a tab is a small flap attached to something

explanation.surface: A choice between a loose flap and a drum, perhaps on a tent.
explanation.definitionFit: A tabor is a small drum, historically played with a pipe by one musician.

clue.text: Wind of change abhorrent? No sailor

indicators.note: the letters of the word abhorrent undergo change, a rearrangement, once the sailor is taken away

parts.note: AB, able-bodied seaman, is the usual abbreviation for a sailor

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a political wind of change is abhorrent, and a sailor says no.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No sailor' asks you to remove AB from ABHORRENT; 'of change' rearranges the remaining HORRENT into a wind from the north.
explanation.definitionFit: A norther is a strong cold wind blowing from the north, especially in Texas and the Gulf of Mexico.

clue.text: Palace in Progress

parts.note: Progress is Bunyan's The Pilgrim's Progress, in which Christian stays at a palace with a famous name

explanation.surface: A palace currently being built or worked on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in Progress' looks like 'under construction', but Progress is the book: Bunyan's The Pilgrim's Progress, where Christian lodges at the Palace Beautiful.
explanation.definitionFit: In The Pilgrim's Progress the House or Palace Beautiful is where Christian rests on his journey.

clue.text: But it ain't hay at this party

definitions.text: But it ain't hay at this party

parts.words: But it ain't hay at this party
parts.note: plays on the old phrase a needle in a ___ of hay, while at a party of this name every guest brings wine or beer instead

explanation.surface: Someone at a rural party insists it is not the haystack that matters here.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverbial search was for a needle 'in a bottle of hay' (bottle being an old word for a bundle); at a bottle party guests bring drink, not hay.
explanation.definitionFit: A bottle party is one where each guest contributes a bottle of drink.

clue.text: Set upon, being very musical, came first

parts.note: assai is the Italian musical direction meaning very, as in allegro assai
led means came first, was in front

explanation.surface: A very musical person triumphed at a competition, coming first.
explanation.walkthrough: ASSAI is a tempo marking on a score meaning 'very'; 'being' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Assailed means attacked, set upon violently.

clue.text: Sob-stuff troublemakers find moving

parts.note: the sob-stuff is a chemical that makes eyes water, and police use it to move rioting troublemakers on

explanation.surface: Agitators are touched by sentimental tear-jerking material.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving' seems to mean emotionally touching, as with a weepie, but the stuff literally makes rioters weep and disperse.
explanation.definitionFit: Tear gas is an irritant that makes the eyes stream, used for crowd control.

clue.text: Style of book I have in such early years

parts.note: the format of a book is its size, shape and style of make-up
I have contracts to I've

explanation.surface: A book about my childhood is written in a particular style.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition describes childhood years as those that shape the person; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Childhood is called the formative years because they shape character and development.

clue.text: What good capon did, in justice, for a corporation

definitions.text: What good capon did, in justice, for a corporation

parts.words: What good capon did, in justice, for a corporation
parts.note: quotes Jaques's seven ages speech in As You Like It, where the justice has a fair round belly with good capon filled inside it

explanation.surface: A question of what a fine fowl achieved, in fairness, for a business company.
explanation.walkthrough: A corporation is old slang for a paunch; in As You Like It the justice's belly is 'with good capon lin'd'. 'justice' and 'corporation' both pretend to be legal and commercial words.
explanation.definitionFit: Lined means filled the inside of, as rich food fills a belly.

clue.text: Yes, it's rough round the bar for luxury lovers

indicators.note: round means the scrambled letters go around the outside of the bar
rough means the letters are roughed up, put in disorder

parts.note: the apostrophe is ignored, giving the letters as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A pub-goer agrees that things get rough around the bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rough' rearranges YES and ITS into SYITES, and 'round' wraps those letters around BAR; 'the' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Sybarites are people devoted to pleasure and comfort, after the luxurious ancient city of Sybaris.

clue.text: The stage for kitchen-sink drama ?

parts.note: names both a theatre's front stage area and a garment worn while washing up at the kitchen sink

explanation.surface: Asks where gritty working-class theatre is performed.
explanation.walkthrough: Kitchen-sink drama is realist British theatre of the 1950s; the answer is both the part of the stage in front of the curtain and what you wear at the sink.
explanation.definitionFit: An apron is the forestage in front of the proscenium, and also a protective garment for kitchen work.

clue.text: Many a hard girl's left mixed training ground

indicators.note: mixed means the preceding letters are jumbled together into a new order

parts.note: the apostrophe is dropped and the S kept

explanation.surface: Many a tough girl has quit a coeducational training camp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'training ground' looks like a sports field, but it is a place where railway trains are put together.
explanation.definitionFit: A marshalling yard is a railway yard where wagons are sorted and assembled into trains.

clue.text: Club recommended for a rake?

explanation.surface: Membership of a London club is advised for a dissolute man.
explanation.walkthrough: The Reform Club is a famous London gentlemen's club on Pall Mall; a rake (a dissolute man) is urged to mend his ways.
explanation.definitionFit: The Reform is a Pall Mall club, and to mend one's ways is what a libertine is advised to do.

clue.text: Musicians remedy its faults

indicators.note: to remedy faults is to put things right, here by putting the letters into a new order

explanation.surface: Players in an orchestra correct its errors.
explanation.definitionFit: Flautists are players of the flute.

clue.text: Holding the beast (having a sort of bone in one's leg ?)

indicators.note: in means these letters are placed inside the word for one's limb

parts.note: taken as written
the shin is the front of the leg, the shinbone

explanation.surface: Someone restrains an animal, perhaps with a bone set in its leg.
explanation.walkthrough: A and SHIN go 'in' LEG; 'having' and 'one's' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Leashing means holding an animal on a lead or strap.

clue.text: Bird walk in old Berlin ?

parts.note: a march named after a farmyard bird, the stiff-legged parade step of soldiers under the Nazis

explanation.surface: Asks how a bird strolls in the German capital of former days.
explanation.walkthrough: The march of Nazi troops, with legs swung high and straight, was named after a waterfowl's gait.
explanation.definitionFit: The goose-step is a marching style with straight legs raised high, associated with German military parades.

clue.text: Correcting the sound script

indicators.note: the sound tells you to go by how the word for script is pronounced, not spelt

parts.note: writing means handwriting, script

explanation.surface: Someone is editing a film's soundtrack and script.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the sound' looks like a film soundtrack but signals that WRITING is said aloud.
explanation.definitionFit: Righting means setting right, putting a wrong to rights.

clue.text: Fur coat money's in the main family

parts.note: the main is a poetic term for the open ocean
L stands for pound sterling, libra, plus the S of the possessive
kin means family, relations

explanation.surface: A wealthy family has its money tied up in a fur coat.
explanation.walkthrough: SEA (the main) plus L'S plus KIN; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Sealskin is the fur of the seal, made into coats.

clue.text: Flowering shrub no good initially in an Arab republic

indicators.note: in means the picked letters go inside the name of the state

parts.note: Syria is a republic in the Arab world

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of no and of good

explanation.surface: A flowering plant does not do well at first in a Middle Eastern country.
explanation.walkthrough: The first letters of 'no good', N and G, go 'in' SYRIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Syringa is the mock orange (and also the botanical genus of lilac), a shrub with fragrant flowers.

clue.text: Take a good look, buddy, at the belvedere

parts.note: to gaze is to look long and steadily
bo is American slang for a pal or buddy

explanation.surface: Someone urges a friend to admire a viewing tower.
explanation.walkthrough: BO is an Americanism for 'buddy', familiar from crosswords; 'at' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A gazebo is a summerhouse or turret with a view, which is what a belvedere is.

clue.text: Settles account for the archdeacon in plenty of time

indicators.note: in means the cleric's title goes inside the long period

parts.note: ages means a long time
an archdeacon is styled the Venerable, abbreviated Ven

explanation.surface: An archdeacon takes a long time to settle his bills.
explanation.walkthrough: 'account' reads as a bill, but 'settles account for' means takes revenge for.
explanation.definitionFit: To avenge a wrong is to exact retribution for it, settling the score.

clue.text: Sententious, like those Swiss financiers?

explanation.surface: Swiss bankers are said to speak in pithy aphorisms.
explanation.walkthrough: Zurich bankers were dubbed 'the gnomes of Zurich' by a British politician in the 1960s; the word also means given to pithy maxims.
explanation.definitionFit: Sententious and the first sense both describe aphoristic, maxim-laden speech; the second is the adjective from the gnomes of Zurich.

clue.text: Like spare parts of green table china if broken

indicators.note: if broken means the words are smashed to pieces and the letters put back in a new order

explanation.surface: A green china table service, if smashed, can be replaced like spare parts.
explanation.definitionFit: Spare parts are interchangeable: one can be swapped in for another identical piece.

clue.text: He's honest,' with 'some reservation …

parts.note: plays on the old phrase honest ___ and on a Native American reservation

explanation.surface: Someone is described as truthful, but only with reservations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with some reservation' sounds like a hedge, but means living on a reservation; the old phrase 'honest Injun' is now regarded as offensive.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is an old, now offensive term for a Native American, as in the phrase pledging honesty.

clue.text: … this' warrior

parts.note: continues the previous clue: the reservation man is a young Native American fighter

explanation.surface: Continues the previous clue, naming the honest man as a fighter.
explanation.walkthrough: Read with the clue before it: the man from the reservation is a Native American warrior.
explanation.definitionFit: A brave is a Native American warrior.

clue.text: Hero recovered a special 27's coat

parts.note: the Greek hero who sailed in the Argo to fetch the golden fleece of a ram

explanation.surface: A hero has had a special animal's coat reupholstered.
explanation.walkthrough: 27 across gives the animal; its special coat is the Golden Fleece, retrieved by the leader of the Argonauts.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the leader of the Argonauts won the Golden Fleece from Colchis.

clue.text: I am Bond's boss, I admit, though a non-native

parts.note: I am contracts to I'm
M is James Bond's chief in the Ian Fleming novels
to grant is to admit or concede

explanation.surface: A newcomer confesses to being James Bond's superior.
explanation.walkthrough: 'though' is a link joining the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An immigrant is someone who has come to live in a country not their own.

clue.text: Clings to a perverse longing for the past?

indicators.note: perverse means turned awry, so these letters are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone clings to a contrary yearning for old times.
explanation.definitionFit: Nostalgic describes wistful longing for times gone by.

clue.text: She has record followers

parts.note: taken as written
EP, extended play, is a type of record

explanation.surface: A woman has her own fan base, perhaps from a hit record.
explanation.walkthrough: 'followers' suggests fans of a singer, but means meek animals that follow the flock; 'has' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: These farm animals are proverbial for blindly following one another.
